matches.title: Fire Flux Esports vs. Noir Verse
matches.tournament: CCT 2026 Challengers Europe Series 6 (Sep 5-13), 16-team double-elim playoff bracket, BO3, online EU, ~$2,500
matches.headline: Stable Turkish core vs a two-week-old Noir Verse lineup priced like the old one
matches.analysis: HLTV has these six spots apart (#143 vs #149) and Polymarket is a coin flip (NOI 1.82 / FIRE 1.89), so the whole question is which side of that the roster evidence sits. Fire Flux have fielded Cizzx, Quality-, zer0UKY, xEternaLxx and zemix unchanged since 21 Mar, and they play a level up: ESL Challenger League Europe (beat Entropy 2-1, lost close ones to Virtus.pro and Inner Circle Academy), ESEA Advanced, runner-up at the ESEA S57 Europe Finals. Noir Verse's rank rise from #188 to #149 was earned 14-23 Aug in this exact CCT Challengers bracket - headlined by a 2-1 upset of ENCE - but that run was with fostar, who left on 24 Aug. Since deeN replaced him they forfeited a Fiesta Series 1 fixture 'unable to field an eligible roster', had another cancelled, and were beaten 0-2 by HAVU on 1 Sep. Transitively Fire Flux beat WBT 2-0 in June and WBT beat Noir Verse 2-1 on 23 Aug; both beat Entropy. The honest offset is the veto: Noir Verse permaban Inferno, Fire Flux's best map at 71%. Lean Fire Flux, not a conviction bet.

matches.headline: Bookmakers make ASCEND a 1.46 favourite; SINQU Rehti's roster was gutted in July
matches.analysis: Two tier-5 sides, neither HLTV-ranked, near-identical ELO (991 vs ~997). Kalshi's 0.12/0.54 both ways is an empty book, so the only real price is the bookmaker line: TEAM ASCEND 1.46, SINQU Rehti 2.54 (~63/37). My own read is closer to even. Against ASCEND: they went 1-3 (13th/16) in the Exort 29 Contenders group against tier-4/5 opposition, are a rotating Spanish pickup five (kr0wa/KaonGod/fix/zeiT/m0t11/NinjaT1/lucibesten across three events), and have no confirmed match since 4 Jul. Against SINQU Rehti: the org promoted MikOne, imbaemba, Eem3l1 and coach Louna to the SINQU main roster in July, leaving 0njib/wejkko plus revu/vrt/xeNi/KapiV; in EPL Regular Season 6 they went 0-2 (1-4 in maps) and had to use coach-level stand-ins on individual maps. That is a genuinely degraded, unsettled team on a four-series losing run. I side with the price plus the roster-damage story, but only just — this is a coin flip with a lean.

matches.analysis: Tier-3 NA online BO1, NSTLGA S2 Swiss round 3, both 1-1 and needing the win. Six days ago at FRAG Midwest St. Louis (LAN) For Fun swept Wanted Goons 2-0 — Nuke 13-6 plus a closer Ancient — and finished 3rd there (beat Kodex 2-0, regain 2-1, 30yo talents 2-0) while WG exited 5th-6th. Valve global points agree: For Fun 813 (#152) vs WG 685, even though HLTV's stale world ranking has WG #194 and For Fun unranked, which is likely why books price WG at 1.66. WG's HLTV lineup tonight is febreeze/twigs/Johan/killerPandas/hibui — Magic out, twigs a stand-in with under five maps with the core — and that five just lost 7-13 to Iowa Stormboar. For Fun's round-2 loss (5-13 to SportsBetExpert, the field's top seed) is the softer defeat. WG's map profile is poor almost everywhere (Mirage 37.5%, Nuke 33%, Ancient 44%, Inferno and Anubis 0%), and For Fun already beat them on two of the likelier BO1 landing spots. Clear lean to For Fun, but it is a BO1 on thin tier-3 data, so roughly 60% rather than anything firmer.

matches.headline: FOKUS higher-ranked, won the H2H, and beat HOTU who 2-0'd Nemiga this week
matches.analysis: Semifinal of the Stake Ranked Ep4 closed qualifier, BO3 online, two slots to a $100k LAN — both sides fully motivated. Rosters matter here: FOKUS rebuilt in mid-July (Jorko to Liquid, podi in Jul 14; volt out, jocab in Jul 16) and Nemiga rebuilt even more recently (robo for 1eeR Jul 17, Xant3r back for sowalio Aug 15), so the lone H2H (FOKUS 2-1, May 31) predates both fives. FOKUS is #41 to Nemiga's #63, has the better ceiling with this exact five (2-1 upset of Aurora at BLAST Bounty Summer; kuben coaching), and beat HOTU (#28) 2-1 on Sep 5 — the same HOTU that 0-2'd Nemiga on Sep 2. Against that, Nemiga are the form team: 4 straight series wins, 2-1 over BIG (#23), 2-0 over Acend (#39) where FOKUS lost 1-2, and Mirage looks like their best map. Genuinely close; I take the higher-ranked, better-tested side by a nose.

matches.title: NIP vs. fnatic
matches.tournament: Stake Ranked Episode 4 Closed Qualifier (StarLadder), semi-final = direct LAN qualification match, BO3, online (EU)
matches.headline: NIP's IGL is four days old; fnatic are drilled, in rhythm and won the VP chain
matches.analysis: Closed-qualifier semi: the winner takes a Stake Ranked Ep4 LAN spot, the loser gets nothing, so motivation is level and maximal. NIP are higher ranked (#26 v #38) and have the best player on the server in stavn (1.63 in Saturday's quarter-final), but their five is half-temporary: Snappi stepped down Aug 31, Krimbo came in on loan from BIG as IGL on Sep 2, and n0te is still an academy stand-in filling cairne's old slot -- cairne now plays for fnatic. Four days of a new IGL's system is thin structure for a BO3 against a side that has won five straight: fnatic came through the open qualifier, beat Virtus.pro 2-1 and BBL 2-1, and made a LAN semi-final at Stake Pulse Beat I a month ago while climbing from #115 in April to #38. The one clean transitive line agrees -- fnatic beat VP 2-1 on Sep 3, NIP lost to the same VP 1-2 in July. H2H is stale (last meeting Jun 2025, no shared players). It stays close because NIP's firepower is real and they have already won two BO3s with Krimbo, so this is a lean, not a conviction bet.

matches.headline: Brute rebuilt 3 days ago; ASTRAL stable since March and ranked higher
matches.analysis: Group D opener of the Logitech G Play Connect closed qualifier — BO3, online, with a $100k Poland LAN behind it. The price is 50/50 because the market is anchored on Jul 28, when Brute beat ASTRAL 2-1 in the Urban Riga Open #6 final and took the title. That Brute no longer exists: majky was benched Aug 27 and tAk arrived on loan from G2 Ares Aug 28, the seventh roster move since March. ASTRAL's five (gxx-, swiz, RaY5ive, meowpop, Neqy) has been intact since Mar 16. Both rating systems put ASTRAL ahead — HLTV #91 vs #109, GosuGamers #101 vs #117 — and the one clean shared opponent leans the same way: ASTRAL beat NAVI Junior 2-0 on LAN Jul 28, Brute lost 0-2 to them Aug 7 (though Brute did win a BO1 against them Jul 27). Against that, tAk is a real player, not a warm body: 1.18 rating in 2026 as G2 Ares' star, with brief tier-1 time at IEM Rio. He may simply be the best gun on the server. So this is a lean, not a lock — a 2-3 day-old lineup usually loses more in defaults and veto depth than it gains in raw aim.

The 0.59 on Lavked reads like a pure rating-model output (GosuGamers ELO 1033 v 974, Strafe #110 v #124) and it underweights two things. First, HAVU won the Aug 18 meeting with these exact fives: Lavked forfeited Ancient at 0-8 on technical issues, then lost Nuke 13-9, so the one competitively played map went HAVU's way. Second, Nuke is Lavked's habit pick (~76% pick rate, ~36% win rate) and it is HAVU's strongest map right now, 3-1 in the last fortnight. Lavked are also 0-3 on Inferno and 0-2 on Ancient since Aug 19, and HAVU's five has been together since Jan 2025 (8Juho8 since Jun 29) against a Lavked lineup 24 days old. Against that, the Black Phoenix chain is genuine and points at Lavked. Net I make it close to even, roughly 52/48 Lavked, which makes HAVU at 0.42 the side holding the price. A value play, not a conviction play: no stand-in, no format mispricing, nothing decisive either way, hence no medal.

rows.headline: NOVAQ are 3-0 vs Rune Eaters in 2026 and rank level, yet priced as 38% underdogs
rows.analysis: Two Kazakh teams, effectively level on paper: HLTV's Aug 17 ranking has NOVAQ #87 and Rune Eaters #88, and Valve's Sep 1 list separates them by 12 points. Yet the market prices RUN at ~61.5%. The head-to-head is one-way: NOVAQ have won all three 2026 meetings 2-1 (Feb 26 MPL S2, Jun 25 LG UltraGear LAN, Jul 26 Ertis Cup grand final), the last two with the exact five they field here (neaLaN, Pump, tasman, AdreN, nyx + coach keeN). Map-level, NOVAQ have taken the Dust2 decider both times (13-10, 13-8) and hammered Mirage 13-5; RUN's edge is Inferno and Ancient. Meanwhile RUN are the ones who changed: dukefissura came in as captain/IGL on Aug 22, kumao was benched Aug 23, and they have had no coach since Jul 30 - a 12-day-old lineup priced like a settled favourite. The honest offset is that RUN are match-sharp (advanced from Group B on Aug 28, 13-5 Ancient over G2 Ares) and climbing fast (#144 in May), while NOVAQ have not played an official match since Jul 26. That caps this at a lean, not a lock - but 38% is too cheap for the team that keeps winning this fixture.

rows.headline: Tougher schedule and the Sashi chain give FOKUS a hair in a genuine coin-flip BO3
rows.analysis: A coin flip on the board and close to one in reality, with a thin lean to FOKUS. Both sit in the same band (FOKUS #41, SINNERS #50) and both were 0-2'd by #212 ex-Zero Tenacity within 48 hours of each other, so the ugly recent results cancel. The separator is strength of schedule: FOKUS's 25% 30-day win rate came against MOUZ, Astralis, Heroic, Acend (#43) and Aurora - they beat Aurora 2-1 with the current five - while SINNERS' healthier ledger is built on Bushido Wildcats, Dark Tigre, MANGANESE, INOX and EAC. The one clean chain agrees: FOKUS 2-0 over Sashi (#44) on Aug 8, SINNERS 1-2 to that same Sashi in the CCT EU #5 final on Aug 2. FOKUS's July rebuild (podi for Jorko, jocab for volt) reads as a talent injection rather than a downgrade, and at seven weeks and roughly ten series it is past the danger window. SINNERS' counter-case is real - 14 months of continuity, a LORGAR S1 LAN title in April, and match sharpness against a FOKUS side that has played one series in 24 days - which is why this is 54/46 and not more.

rows.analysis: Verified grand final, BO3, online OCE, 09:00 UTC — winner takes $1,500 and the Asia-Pacific Finals slot, so no dead rubber. THUNDER lost IGL/AWPer aliStair on Aug 27 and has signed nobody; Liquipedia still lists four players plus coach viridian, with Singaporean AWPer Gratisfaction standing in. That headline scares people, but it has already been road-tested: the patched five beat Mindfreak 2-0 on Aug 28 and beat this exact Ground Zero side 2-1 on Aug 30, +21 rounds across three maps (Nuke 13-5, Inferno 12-13, Anubis 13-3). THUNDER is the better team underneath — #2 in Australia to GZ's #3, an IEM Cologne Major Stage 1 attendee, roster of Liazz/dexter/asap/TjP. The veto is GZ's structural problem: their bans run Cache then Ancient, leaving Anubis — THUNDER's 79% map over 19 maps — as the decider, exactly how Aug 30 played out. GZ's counter-case is real: stable since June 10, warm off a 2-0 over Arcade, they stole Inferno 13-12, and they won this identical LB-revenge grand final against THUNDER at the July LAN. Close, but the direct evidence and the map pool point the same way.

rows.analysis: Verified as the Cup 5 Group D decider: csdb.gg and GosuGamers both show Permitta vs Azuolas, Aug 31 13:00 UTC, BO3, online EU — a rematch of yesterday's opener, which Permitta won 2-0 (Ancient 13-11, Mirage 16-12 OT). Both then split: Permitta swept 0-2 by WBT in the winners' match, Azuolas edged BERG 2-1. Permitta are ~#109 with an established Polish core (AdrieN, Markos, maaryy, tomiko + showk, the los kogutos five re-signed Aug 13, pako coaching); Azuolas are an unranked, brand-new all-Lithuanian roster (matyA, yakuza, MAGILA, StreakN, Uzman) with only those two series on record anywhere. The same-day, same-roster 2-0 is the best evidence available and points one way, but it was tight — 23 rounds to 29 over two maps — and a two-step chain (both Azuolas and WBT beat BERG 2-1; WBT then 2-0'd Permitta) argues Azuolas sit in the same band. Permitta's own map data is a mild drag: Ancient 25% over 90 days is their own pick, while Cache (83%) is what Azuolas ban. Fair around 62%, nowhere near the ~0.79 ask, so no medal.

The ugly recent line (4-13 to unranked Color, Aug 24) was a BO1 open qualifier, the noisiest sample there is; their Cup 3 losses to Fire Flux and BASEMENT BOYS were both 1-2 BO3s, and they took Virtus.pro to three maps on LAN. The two are dead level on Valve's Americas list — EMPIRE #58/639, Overtake #59/631 — and have never met. rows.headline: Near-identical ELO and a 1-1 H2H make 0.42 the better-priced side in a thin market
rows.analysis: Two unranked tier-3 sides who have met twice in three weeks with these exact rosters: INFURITY won 2-1 on Aug 11 (S53 UB SF), Teletubisie won 2-0 on Aug 14 (S53 LB Final) to eliminate them, then took the title. Both rosters are settled -- INFURITY's CHANKY/AwaykeN joined May 29, Teletubisie's Polish five (byali, Dycha, mASKED, POLO, Sobol) unchanged through August -- so no stand-in edge exists. GosuGamers ELO has them nearly level (1007 vs 1012, #89 vs #84 world), yet Kalshi prices Teletubisie ~0.595 mid. Teletubisie deserves the lean: better form (4-1 last five, S53 champion), the decisive H2H, and the WOPA chain. I make it roughly 56/44. That still leaves INFURITY the better-priced side at a 0.42 ask, while Teletubisie at 0.64 is worse than fair. This is a price lean on a 9-cent spread with 11 total contracts traded, not a thesis about the better team -- hence no medal and low confidence.

G2 beat that same M80 side at EWC, went unbeaten through their EWC group, beat Astralis 2-1 in the Ro16 and lost only to FURIA 1-2 in the quarters; here they beat Aurora 2-0 and lost only to #1 Spirit. G2 also lead the 2026 H2H 2-1, taking the last two, including June's Major decider where NAVI coughed up a 12-8 Inferno lead. Rankings favour OG (#61 vs #78, Aug 24) yet the market has EF at ~54% on both Kalshi and Polymarket (1.82 vs 2.17) — it has already absorbed the news, which is why this is ungraded. The news is real: on Aug 23 EF benched br0 (0.93 over 21 maps) for soulfly, an ex-Aurora rifler with a 1.01 rating, an EPL S23 final and an IEM Cologne Major semi behind him, and made jottAAA permanent. OG went 3-1 in ESL Challenger League S52 Cup 4 but lost the final 1-2 to #90 Metizport, and were swept 0-2 by BC.Game at the EWC open qualifier. Second, Nuke is Lavked's habit pick (~76% pick rate, ~36% win rate) and it is HAVU's strongest map right now, 3-1 in the last fortnight. Against that, the Black Phoenix chain is genuine and points at Lavked. Net I make it close to even, roughly 52/48 Lavked, which makes HAVU at 0.42 the side holding the price. A value play, not a conviction play: no stand-in, no format mispricing, nothing decisive either way, hence no medal.

rows.headline: Tougher schedule and the Sashi chain give FOKUS a hair in a genuine coin-flip BO3

Both sit in the same band (FOKUS #41, SINNERS #50) and both were 0-2'd by #212 ex-Zero Tenacity within 48 hours of each other, so the ugly recent results cancel. The separator is strength of schedule: FOKUS's 25% 30-day win rate came against MOUZ, Astralis, Heroic, Acend (#43) and Aurora - they beat Aurora 2-1 with the current five - while SINNERS' healthier ledger is built on Bushido Wildcats, Dark Tigre, MANGANESE, INOX and EAC. The one clean chain agrees: FOKUS 2-0 over Sashi (#44) on Aug 8, SINNERS 1-2 to that same Sashi in the CCT EU #5 final on Aug 2. FOKUS's July rebuild (podi for Jorko, jocab for volt) reads as a talent injection rather than a downgrade, and at seven weeks and roughly ten series it is past the danger window. SINNERS' counter-case is real - 14 months of continuity, a LORGAR S1 LAN title in April, and match sharpness against a FOKUS side that has played one series in 24 days - which is why this is 54/46 and not more.

rows.analysis: Both sides are unranked tier-4 teams in the United21 S54 upper-bracket final (BO3, online EU, $10k). Teletubisie is far more proven: a stable Polish five (byali, Dycha, mASKED, POLO, Sobol) unchanged since S53, where they reached the grand final and lost 1-2 to WOPA. In S54 they beat Alliance 2-0, ENCE Prospects 2-0, B8 Academy 2-1 and INFURITY 2-0; on Aug 29-30 they beat HAVU 13-4 on Nuke and took Cache off a fnatic lineup in a 104-team open qualifier. QUB is near-blank: about five tracked series ever, no Liquipedia team page, somnium in for qSniff around Aug 15, a 0-2 group loss to a weak LPH Gaming and a BO1 exit to Young TigeRES. Their 2-0 sweeps of Phantom Academy and EAC Rising are real, and the Phantom chain is the best case for QUB. Map pool leans Teletubisie: Nuke and Cache are their picks and QUB has zero tracked Nuke maps; QUB's Mirage is Teletubisie's soft spot, so expect a decider on Ancient or Dust II where Teletubisie is stronger. rows.analysis: BO3 LAN at BLAST's Copenhagen studio, Group B upper-bracket final; both are already through to Porto, so this only decides the group-1 bye to the playoff semis. Rosters settled and verified: Falcons (karrigan/NiKo/m0NESY/TeSeS/kyousuke, together since 20 Apr) and MOUZ (torzsi/Spinx/xertioN/xelex/PR, PR signed 14 Jul). MOUZ are genuinely hot: BLAST Bounty S2 champions on 2 Aug (3-1 over Spirit) and 4-0 in maps here averaging 13-5 — but those sweeps came against 9z (#12) and unranked Inner Circle, while Falcons' 2-1 over Legacy (#7) is the better scalp at this event. Falcons' only two map losses in Copenhagen are both Ancient (10-13 twice); on everything else they are 4-0 at 13-4/13-9/13-6/13-6, and karrigan will not leave Ancient open against MOUZ. Against that: Falcons lost 1-2 to 100 Thieves and 0-2 to Legacy since the Major, and only m0NESY cleared 1.00 in the EWC exit. The 754-vs-512 points gap plus firepower puts Falcons near 56%; at 0.54 ask that is a ~2-point edge, so small size, no medal.

rows.headline: Bushido #73 and 5-1 here; NPG #106 reached the semi on a forfeit
rows.analysis: Exort Fiesta Series 1 semi-final, BO3, online EU, 11:00 UTC. Bushido (#73, career high, up from #121 in early Aug) earned this: 3-1 in Swiss, then 2-0 over Metizport (Mirage 13-9, Nuke 13-4) and 2-0 over Endless Journey. Nordic Partners (#106) are here on a bracket gift — their Ro16 was a forfeit (benched gods 'unable to field an eligible roster'; Liquipedia bracket shows score=FF), so they have played one real series in the event. Their actual ledger is 1-4 in three weeks: 0-3 at NODWIN Clutch Series 11 (BET-M 1-2, Black Phoenix 1-2, GenOne 0-2) plus 0-2 to GenOne on Aug 5; the 2-1 over Walczaki as a 3.23 dog is the outlier. Map depth favours BW: 6-0 on Dust II in three weeks (NPG lost it 2-13 and 9-13) and strong on Mirage and Nuke, while NPG have one data point each on their good maps and were blown out 3-13 on Inferno. NPG's five is 34 days old; BW's has a 15-month core. Caveats: BW lost 1-2 to UNiTY hours ago and have been coachless since ekg left Aug 28, and k1to is the best player on the server.

GamePoint is ~#213, an 11% career win rate per GosuGamers, currently on a ~5-loss slide (ELO 985), with signs of churn in a roster only formed in May (match card lists dako and bekushima in place of slash/shoma — unverified). Books price this ~1.83/1.87, a coin flip, because GamePoint swept DEPO 2-0 on Aug 9 during their run to the Summer Battle Cup final — the only meeting versus DEPO's current five, and it caps my number. But DEPO crushed the May meeting 13-1/13-8, made two finals in the same August window (BRO Summer Cup, losing only to #114 Omega), and BO3 favors the deeper, more experienced side. Fundamentals say ~57% DEPO; the market's evens line looks slightly cheap on the better team, but the data is tier-4 thin and contradictory, so this is a lean, not an edge — ungraded, small.

On paper they are tied: HLTV world ~#101 Rare Atom vs ~#107 NEXVOID, while Valve's Asia regional ranking (Aug 25) has NEXVOID 1124 pts to RA 1108. Both arrived 3-0. The separator is map form. NEXVOID have gone Inferno 13-1 and 13-5, Ancient 13-5, 13-6 and 13-9, Anubis 13-8 this week - six map wins averaging +7.3 rounds, their only regulation loss an OT Nuke on Chinggis Warriors' pick. Rare Atom's run is scrappier: they dropped their own Cache pick 6-13 to The Huns and needed 16-14 plus a triple-OT 22-19 Mirage to survive, and in the Moscow qualifier they lost Inferno 8-13 and Ancient 11-13 to 5star. RA can ban Inferno, but Ancient then sits as NEXVOID's likely pick or the decider - exactly where the gap is widest. Bookmakers priced NEXVOID 1.54 vs Chinggis Warriors on Aug 28 against RA 1.68 vs comparable-tier The Huns, a mild echo. Against that, RA beat The Huns 13-0/13-3 on Aug 22, the best single series either side has produced. A thin lean, not an edge.

rows.headline: EF's Aug 23 soulfly upgrade already beat #31 100T; OG lost a final to #90 Metizport
rows.analysis: Online BO3, Group C opener of the Logitech G Play Connect closed qualifier (feeds a $100k Warsaw LAN). Rankings favour OG (#61 vs #78, Aug 24) yet the market has EF at ~54% on both Kalshi and Polymarket (1.82 vs 2.17) — it has already absorbed the news, which is why this is ungraded. The news is real: on Aug 23 EF benched br0 (0.93 over 21 maps) for soulfly, an ex-Aurora rifler with a 1.01 rating, an EPL S23 final and an IEM Cologne Major semi behind him, and made jottAAA permanent. In soulfly's debut the next day, #78 EF beat #31 100 Thieves 2-1 to reach the IEM Beijing closed qualifier, taking the decider 13-10 from 6-10 down. rows.analysis: Sashi (#47) is the better team and the fresher one. Their August includes the CCT Europe S5 title (2-1 over SINNERS in the final) and a 2-1 upset of Virtus.pro en route to 5-8th at the EWC Open Qualifier — a ceiling INOX (#81, peak #50) has never shown. Against that: INOX re-signed gooddeph on Aug 14, restoring the founding five, and the #62-to-#81 slide was earned with notineki standing in; they are 4-2 since, with 13-4/13-6/13-7 scorelines. Chains are mixed — SINNERS and Virtus.pro favour Sashi, ex-RUSTEC favours INOX. Veto is near-symmetric: Sashi 4-1 on Cache but 1-4 on Dust II; INOX 4-1 on Inferno. Fair value ~57% against a 0.56 ask is a sliver, not an edge — hence no medal.
